ledger.x: 30 March 1867: the Compromise creates Austria-Hungary.
1878: Austria-Hungary occupies the Sanjak of Novi Pazar.
29 July 1878: Austria-Hungary occupies Bosnia and Herzegovina.
27 December 1902: the concession 'formally began' (the infobox says 'Established: 1901'; the article elsewhere says it was obtained 'after the signing of the Boxer Protocol').
5-7 October 1908: the occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina becomes annexation.

5 October 1908: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina, 'establishing the Condominium of Bosnia and Herzegovina'; the Ottoman Empire recognised the annexation 'on 26 February 1909' (Austria-Hungary page: 'Bosnian Crisis: 6 October 1908').
1909: the Sanjak of Novi Pazar returns to the Ottoman Empire.
1914: Russia invades Galicia.

1914: the same Russian invasion, for the remainder of Galicia and Bukovina that Cliopatria's 1916 shape still lacks and that Russia held until 1917 (the Brusilov Offensive of June 1916 forced the Austro-Hungarian 2nd and 3rd Armies back again).
May 1915: the Central Powers' offensive retakes Galicia.

1 September 1915: the Austro-Hungarian Military General Government of Lublin (infobox 'Established: 1 September 1915'; the army formed it on 25 August 1915 as the 'General Government of Kielce'; seat Kielce, then Lublin).
6 October 1915: the Central Powers invade Serbia.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 24 November 1915: the Serbian campaign ends.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: Autumn 1915: Serbia is occupied.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 8 January 1916: Austria-Hungary attacks Mount Lovcen.
17 January 1916: Montenegro falls.
January 1916: Montenegro is occupied.
End of February 1916: Austro-Hungarian troops take Scutari and Durazzo.
27 August 1916: Romania invades Transylvania.
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: 25 October 1916: 'by 25 October the Romanian army was back to its initial positions' (Romanian Campaign page).
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: 6 December 1916: Bucharest is captured.
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: March 1917 (dossier boundary): the Russian Empire falls (russian-empire dossier /ledger/137, dissolve to russian-republic) and its hold on the remainder of Galicia and Bukovina passes to the Provisional Government, recorded in the next two events.

March 1917 (bridge): the Russian-held remainder of Galicia and Bukovina continues under the Provisional Government, the state that launched the offensive of 29 June 1917 ('Russian Provisional Government'; Kerensky Offensive page).
14 August 1917: China, having declared war on Austria-Hungary and Germany, occupied the concession and declared the concessions 'revoked on 14 August 1917'; it was handed over at 16:00 that day.

3 August 1917: 'The Germans launched their counteroffensive against the Southwestern Front on 19 July', 'Austro-German troops took the city of Tarnopol on 25 July' and Czernowitz 'fell on 3 August'; 'Most of the Austro-Hungarian provinces of Galicia and Bukovina were retaken'; Kornilov stabilised the front 'by…
24 October 1917: the Austrians break through at Caporetto.

18 February 1918: Operation Faustschlag (infobox '18 February - 3 March 1918'): 'the German and Austro-Hungarian forces started a major three-pronged offensive'; 'Ukrainian troops and the Austro-Hungarian Army had secured Odessa'; after Brest-Litovsk 'capturing the whole of Ukraine'.

September 1918: 'In September 1918, the Entente forces broke through the Central Powers' lines north of Thessaloniki, and within days Austro-Hungarian forces began to withdraw from Albania' (Principality of Albania page; the albania dossier /ledger/5 has the same).
October 1918: Austria-Hungary 'occupied Montenegro from 15 January 1916 to October 1918' (Kingdom of Montenegro page; the montenegro dossier /ledger/12 has the same).

28-30 October 1918: Czech politicians take over in Prague (28 October), the Czechs and Slovaks proclaim Czechoslovakia (28 October) and the Slovaks do the same on 30 October; Czechoslovakia is the infobox successor.
29 October 1918: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is proclaimed; the page's sentence names 'the Slavs in both portions of what remained of Austria-Hungary'.
ledger.cpn: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs

ledger.x: 31 October 1918: Hungary repudiates the Compromise of 1867 ('On 17 October 1918, the Hungarian Parliament voted in favour of terminating the union with Austria'); 'Karolyi followed suit on 16 November, proclaiming the Hungarian Democratic Republic'.
30 October 1918: German-Austria acts as a state.

28 October 1918: the Polish Liquidation Committee is 'Created on 28 October 1918' by Polish members of the Austrian parliament, seat Krakow, to keep order in 'the former Austrian part of partitioned Poland'; infobox successors of Austria-Hungary: 'Polish Liquidation Committee', 'Kingdom of Poland'.

1 November 1918: 'The West Ukrainian People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 November 1918' at Lviv, 'Until November 13, 1918, the state was officially known as the Ukrainian State'; it 'controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919'.

28 November 1918 (Bukovina) and 1 December 1918 (Transylvania): 'The union of Bukovina with Romania is declared' and 'the union of Transylvania with the Kingdom of Romania on 1 December 1918'; Trianon confirmed 'Transylvania, part of Banat and other territories'.
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: 25 November 1918: the Great National Assembly at Novi Sad 'declared the accession' of 'Banat, Bačka and Baranja' to the Kingdom of Serbia, seceding from the 'already collapsed Austria-Hungary'; Syrmia joined on 24 November (serbs dossier /ledger/28).
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 3 November 1918 (occupation) and 10 September 1919 (treaty): Saint-Germain gave Italy 'The southern half of the former Tyrolean crownland up to the Brenner Pass' and 'the Austrian Littoral', 'the Imperial Free City of Trieste' and Istria; the Villa Giusti armistice was signed on 3 November 1918 (Austria-Hungary page).
31 October 1918: Austria-Hungary dissolves.
1 November 1918: Serbian forces enter Belgrade after the Vardar Offensive of September 1918.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 3 November 1918: the armistice of Villa Giusti.
November 1918 (page silent): the occupation of Wallachia ends with the Central Powers' collapse.
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: November 1918 (page silent): the Austro-Hungarian zone in Ukraine ends with the collapse; no date on the page.
November 1918: infobox 'Armistice, withdrawal of German forces: 3 November 1918'; Governor Anton Liposcak 'resigned on 2 November 1918' after Austria-Hungary dissolved.

wars.name: Occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (1878)
wars.outcome: 'The occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina started on 29 July 1878 and was over on 20 October'; Bosnia stayed Ottoman in law until the annexation of October 1908.

wars.name: Serbian campaign of World War I
wars.outcome: The Central Powers' offensive of 6 October 1915 ended on 24 November 1915; Serbia 'was then occupied and divided between the Austro-Hungarian Empire and Bulgaria'; Serbian forces entered Belgrade on 1 November 1918.

wars.name: Montenegrin campaign
wars.outcome: Austro-Hungarian victory in the infobox dates 5-17 January 1916; Cetinje fell on 13 January, a provisional military government was set up on 1 March, and Scutari and Durazzo were taken at the end of February.

wars.name: Eastern Front (World War I)
wars.outcome: Russia held almost all of Galicia by the end of 1914 and lost it again from May 1915; Romania entered on 27 August 1916 and lost Bucharest on 6 December; the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (3 March 1918) and the Treaty of Bucharest (7 May 1918) closed the front.

wars.name: Italian Front (World War I)
wars.outcome: 'In May 1915, Italy attacked Austria-Hungary'; 'On 24 October 1917, Austrians ... attacked at Caporetto'; the armistice was signed at Villa Giusti on 3 November 1918.

certainty.note: The monarchy's frontiers are treaty lines of the period (the page cites the Congress of Berlin); the Sanjak garrison and the Bosnian occupation (1878-1908) are drawn on the Congress's lines.
The war-years fronts and occupation zones (Galicia, Serbia, Montenegro, Albania, Romania, Italy, Ukraine) are moving or unmapped by the pages; the monarchy's own pre-war frontier stays sharp.
